aphorisms.text: Cynic: A blackguard whose faulty vision sees things as they are, not as they ought to be.
aphorisms.author: Ambrose Bierce

aphorisms.text: Egotist: A person of low taste, more interested in himself than in me.
aphorisms.author: Ambrose Bierce

aphorisms.text: Diplomacy: The patriotic art of lying for one's country.
aphorisms.author: Ambrose Bierce

aphorisms.text: Bore: A person who talks when you wish him to listen.
aphorisms.author: Ambrose Bierce

aphorisms.text: Positive: Being mistaken at the top of one's voice.
aphorisms.author: Ambrose Bierce

aphorisms.text: Alone: In bad company.
aphorisms.author: Ambrose Bierce

aphorisms.text: Acquaintance: A person whom we know well enough to borrow from, but not well enough to lend to.
aphorisms.author: Ambrose Bierce

aphorisms.text: Brain: An apparatus with which we think we think.
aphorisms.author: Ambrose Bierce

aphorisms.text: Conservative: A statesman who is enamored of existing evils, as distinguished from the Liberal, who wishes to replace them with others.
aphorisms.author: Ambrose Bierce

aphorisms.text: Corporation: An ingenious device for obtaining individual profit without individual responsibility.
aphorisms.author: Ambrose Bierce

aphorisms.text: Faith: Belief without evidence in what is told by one who speaks without knowledge, of things without parallel.
aphorisms.author: Ambrose Bierce

aphorisms.text: History: An account mostly false, of events mostly unimportant, which are brought about by rulers mostly knaves, and soldiers mostly fools.
aphorisms.author: Ambrose Bierce

aphorisms.text: Love: A temporary insanity curable by marriage.
aphorisms.author: Ambrose Bierce

aphorisms.text: Marriage: The state or condition of a community consisting of a master, a mistress, and two slaves, making in all, two.
aphorisms.author: Ambrose Bierce

aphorisms.text: Peace: In international affairs, a period of cheating between two periods of fighting.
aphorisms.author: Ambrose Bierce

aphorisms.text: Politeness: The most acceptable hypocrisy.
aphorisms.author: Ambrose Bierce

aphorisms.text: Saint: A dead sinner revised and edited.
aphorisms.author: Ambrose Bierce

aphorisms.text: Self-esteem: An erroneous appraisement.
aphorisms.author: Ambrose Bierce

aphorisms.text: Year: A period of three hundred and sixty-five disappointments.
aphorisms.author: Ambrose Bierce

aphorisms.text: Once: Enough.
aphorisms.author: Ambrose Bierce

aphorisms.text: Quotation: The act of repeating erroneously the words of another.
aphorisms.author: Ambrose Bierce

aphorisms.text: Learning: The kind of ignorance distinguishing the studious.
aphorisms.author: Ambrose Bierce

aphorisms.text: Congratulation: The civility of envy.
aphorisms.author: Ambrose Bierce

aphorisms.text: Admiration: Our polite recognition of another's resemblance to ourselves.
aphorisms.author: Ambrose Bierce

aphorisms.text: Bride: A woman with a fine prospect of happiness behind her.
aphorisms.author: Ambrose Bierce

aphorisms.text: The reports of my death are greatly exaggerated.
